title: Controller exception handling

richText: Handle an exception from a controller
A controller or a service it calls can throw an exception while processing a request.
@ExceptionHandler marks a method that handles a matching exception and returns the HTTP response.
Place a handler in a controller for errors handled only by that controller.
A handler can list several exception classes when they need the same response.
@ControllerAdvice makes its handlers available to controllers across the application.
Advice can also be restricted to selected controller types or packages.
A ResponseEntity return value sets the status, headers and body explicitly.
Controller advice handles errors in Spring MVC request processing. It does not handle every error in the application, such as an exception in an independent background task.

example.title: Return 404 when a user cannot be found
description: Place these public types in separate files in a scanned package.
The controller simulates one existing user with ID 1. Send GET /users/2 with Accept: application/json.
explanation: ID 2 causes find() to throw UserNotFoundException.
Spring selects the matching advice method.
ResponseEntity sets 404. ApiError becomes the JSON response body.
The error message is written by this exception class. Do not expose arbitrary internal exception messages to clients.
example.result:
HTTP status: 404 Not Found
Body: {"message":"User with ID 2 not found"}

richText: Use a status that matches the failure. A missing resource can produce 404; an unexpected server failure normally produces 500.
Use a consistent error body so clients can read it.
Keep stack traces and internal details in server logs. Send a safe message to the client.
Authentication and access failures that occur in Spring Security before controller processing need Spring Security error handlers.

summary: Map controller exceptions to an HTTP status and a response body.
